messages.subject: Flipped, transformed coordinates
parts:
Given this:

TransPow50 <- Trans$new("pow50",function(x) 50^x, function(x) log(x,50), function(x) log(x,50))
d <- structure(list(response = structure(c(5L, 5L, 5L, 5L, 1L, 1L,
1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L), .Label = c("well-labeled, well-formed",
"well-labeled, malformed", "mislabeled, well-formed", "mislabeled, malformed",
"HTTP error"), class = c("ordered", "factor")), count = c(1497L,
466L, 347L, 53L, 178017L, 24445L, 47345L, 5891L, 506L, 332L,
104L, 57L, 424L, 304L, 147L, 74L, 1L, 59L, 0L, 0L), request = structure(c(4L,
2L, 3L, 1L, 4L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 4L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 4L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 4L,
2L, 3L, 1L), .Label = c("cross-origin, quirks mode", "same-origin, quirks mode",
"cross-origin, standard mode", "same-origin, standard mode"), class = c("ordered",
"factor"))), .Names = c("response", "count", "request"), row.names = c(NA,
-20L), class = "data.frame")

I would like to have this plot

ggplot(d, aes(fill=response, x=request, y=count)) +
    geom_bar(position="fill", stat="identity") +
    scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0,0), formatter="percent", breaks=c(.5,.9,.95,.99,1)) +
    scale_x_discrete(expand=c(0,0)) +
    coord_trans(y="pow50") + coord_flip()

that is, *both* exchanging the x- and y-axis, and applying an algebraic transformation to the y-axis (before the flip).  Unfortunately, it appears that only one coord_* function (the last one on the command line) has any effect.  Exchanging x and y throughout gets me only an error message:

Error in if (length(from) == 1 || length(to) == 1 || from[1] == from[2] ||  :
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

and it would be wrong to apply the algebraic transformation to the *data* in this case.  All I want is a filled horizontal barchart with the 0-90% range deemphasized, is that so wrong? ;-)

zw

So I tried to bodge CoordTrans and CoordFlip together.  This is what I have so far:

CoordTransflip <- proto(CoordCartesian, expr={

  new <- function(., xtrans="identity", ytrans="identity") {
    if (is.character(xtrans)) xtrans <- Trans$find(xtrans)
    if (is.character(ytrans)) ytrans <- Trans$find(ytrans)
    .$proto(xtr = xtrans, ytr = ytrans)
  }

  muncher <- function(.) TRUE

  transform <- function(., data, details) {
    trans_x <- function(data) .$transform_x(data, details$x.range)
    trans_y <- function(data) .$transform_y(data, details$y.range)

    data <- transform_position(data, trans_y, trans_x)
    data <- transform_position(data, trim_infinite_01, trim_infinite_01)

    rename(data, c(
      x = "y",       y = "x",
      xend = "yend", yend = "xend",
      xmin = "ymin", ymin = "xmin",
      xmax = "ymax", ymax = "xmax")
    )
  }
  transform_x <- function(., data, range) {
    rescale(.$xtr$transform(data), 0:1, range, clip = FALSE)
  }
  transform_y <- function(., data, range) {
    rescale(.$ytr$transform(data), 0:1, range, clip = FALSE)
  }

  compute_ranges <- function(., scales) {
    trans_range <- function(x, expand) {
      # range is necessary in case transform has flipped min and max
      expand_range(range(x, na.rm = TRUE), expand)
    }

    x.range <- trans_range(.$xtr$transform(scales$x$output_set()),
      scales$x$.expand)
    x.major <- .$transform_x(scales$x$input_breaks_n(), x.range)
    x.minor <- .$transform_x(scales$x$output_breaks(), x.range)
    x.labels <- scales$x$labels()

    y.range <- trans_range(.$ytr$transform(scales$y$output_set()),
      scales$y$.expand)
    y.major <- .$transform_y(scales$y$input_breaks_n(), y.range)
    y.minor <- .$transform_y(scales$y$output_breaks(), y.range)
    y.labels <- scales$y$labels()

    list(
      y.range = x.range, x.range = y.range,
      y.major = x.major, y.minor = x.minor, y.labels = x.labels,
      x.major = y.major, x.minor = y.minor, x.labels = y.labels
    )
  }

  labels <- function(., scales) {
    list(
      x = scales$y,
      y = scales$x
    )
  }

  pprint <- function(., newline=TRUE) {
    cat("coord_", .$objname, ": ",
      "x = ", .$xtr$objname, ", ",
      "y = ", .$ytr$objname, sep = ""
    )
    if (newline) cat("\n")
  }


  # Documentation -----------------------------------------------

  objname <- "transflip"
  desc <- "Transformed, flipped cartesian coordinate system"
  details <- ""
  icon <- function(.) {
    breaks <- cumsum(1 / 2^(1:5))
    gTree(children=gList(
      segmentsGrob(breaks, 0, breaks, 1),
      segmentsGrob(0, breaks, 1, breaks)
    ))
  }
})
coord_transflip <- CoordTransflip$build_accessor()

It doesn't work: with no transformation applied, this *should* be equivalent to coord_flip(), but what I get is a plot background whose limits are all wrong on *both* axes, and with no data on it.  Help?

zw

messages.subject: Re: Flipped, transformed coordinates
parts:
> Not quite the same; that's stacking two coord_trans(), which equates to
> composing the transformers.  I need to stack a coord_trans() and a
> coord_flip(), and I don't believe that can be done by messing with the
> transformers.  Short of bodging together the guts of the internal primitives
> CoordTrans and CoordFlip, I'm really at a loss here...

Doing this in general is tough, because it's not obvious to me that
you should be able to do (e.g.) polar + map or map + polar or flip +
map. Some combinations make sense like flip + polar, polar + flip,
flip + trans, trans + flip, but I'm not sure how they differ from the
previous set. Not mention figuring out how two (or more!) coordinate
systems should interact would be really hard, for something that not
that many people use. (And as it is the coordinate systems don't
interact with facets and scales entirely correctly).

Hadley
